summary: The article argues that financial institutions must manage cybersecurity risks posed by third-party vendors, citing breaches after September 2023 that pushed for stricter regulation. It covers a legislative proposal, expert opinions for and against tighter rules, vendor risk management programs, AI and blockchain tools, and a new regulatory oversight committee. It concludes that collective action combining regulation, best practices and technology is needed.
one_line: Financial institutions face rising cyber risk from third-party vendors, prompting new regulation, risk management programs, technology solutions and an oversight committee.
key_facts: An October 2023 survey of 250 financial organizations found 63% had experienced a data breach indirectly due to vulnerabilities in third-party services.
A November 2023 breach at a major credit bureau compromised the personal data of millions and was linked to a third-party supplier with inadequate security measures.

On December 4, 2023, Senator Elizabeth A. Tiller and Representative John G. Koren jointly proposed legislation for a framework to evaluate the cybersecurity postures of third-party vendors working with financial institutions.
The proposed legislation would mandate periodic audits, enforce industry-standard cybersecurity frameworks, require immediate breach reporting, and impose stiff penalties for non-compliance.
Cybersecurity consultant Meg Henley supports tighter regulation, saying it is about "establishing a culture of cybersecurity resilience that keeps pace with evolving threats."
Financial analyst Robert Langley opposes increased regulation, arguing it could stifle innovation and overburden smaller vendors with compliance costs.

The Federal Financial Institutions Examination Council (FFIEC) launched a third-party vendor risk management (TPVRM) initiative on January 15, 2024, providing guidelines for consistent risk evaluation.
TPVRM programs involve due diligence before onboarding vendors, continuous monitoring, contingency plans, regular audits and certifications, and security education for vendor employees.
Predictive analytics tools using AI and machine learning helped thwart a significant attempted cyberattack on a New York-based bank on February 9, 2024.
On March 6, 2024, a consortium of banks used a blockchain-based platform to streamline vendor risk assessments and securely share risk data.
The Cybersecurity Oversight and Response Committee (CORC), established as of April 2024, oversees enforcement of third-party risk management policies.
CORC conducts routine inspections and reviews incident response plans of financial organizations and their third-party vendors.
